newsitem.title: CHINA: China oil import needs seen at 1.1 mln bpd in 2000.
newsitem.headline: China oil import needs seen at 1.1 mln bpd in 2000.

text.p: China's net oil import requirements are expected to more than double between the years 2000 and 2010, Robert Priddle, executive director of the International Energy Agency (IEA), said on Wednesday.

China's net oil import requirements are forecast to surge to 2.3-3.0 million barrels per day (bpd) by the year 2010 from 1.1 million bpd in 2000, Priddle told a gathering of energy officials, scholars and students from the energy community.
China has been a net oil importer since 1993 and currently imports about 10 percent of its requirements, said Priddle, who is visiting China until November 5.
China imported 17.09 million tonnes (342,000 bpd) of crude in 1995, up 38.4 percent from 1994.

"But it's no more a threat than the import by any other of our member nations. It's simply one of the players in the world demand for oil," Priddle told a news conference when asked if China would become a threat to the world.
Chinese oil production is expected to climb to slightly over 3.0 million bpd by 2000 from close to 3.0 million in 1995, Priddle said.
Output would soar to 3.7-4.5 million bpd by 2010, he added.
"This increase in production is well below China's rising oil demand," Priddle said.
China is the largest oil consumer in Asia after Japan, with annual consumption of 150 million tonnes.

Priddle and China's State Planning Minister Chen Jinhua signed a memorandum of understanding, pledging to cooperate on energy conservation and efficiency, rational and efficient production, extraction, transport, distribution and use of oil, gas, coal, electricity and other sources of energy, including renewables.

The IEA and China also pledged to cooperate on foreign investment and trading in the energy sector, energy supply security, information and statistics, energy research and development and technology deployment, and energy and the environment.
China is the second largest energy-consuming country in the world after the United States.
Currently, China consumes about 10 percent of world energy.

The Paris-based IEA is the forum for coordinating the energy policies of 23 industrialised countries -- Australia, Austria, Belgium, Britain, Canada, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Ireland, Italy, Japan, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Portugal, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkey and the United States.
